definitions.explanation: The deepest, purest black imaginable, evoking the color of Japanese lacquer. A literary term used to describe hair, darkness, or the night sky.

examples.japanese: {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{髪|かみ}→髪：02196_kami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{印象的|いんしょうてき}→印象的：15547_inshouteki⟧だった。
{漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{闇|やみ}→闇：14528_yami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{見|み}えなかった→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: In the pitch-black darkness, I couldn't see anything.

examples.japanese: {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜空|よぞら}→夜空：09591_yozora⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{無数|むすう}→無数：00300_musuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{星|ほし}→星：01510_hoshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧またたき、⟦{息|いき}→息：02176_iki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧ほど⟦{美|うつく}しかった→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
examples.english: Countless stars twinkled in the jet-black night sky, so beautiful it took my breath away.

notes:
A literary word meaning the deepest, purest black — like the color of Japanese lacquer (⟦{漆|うるし}→漆：10584_urushi⟧). Combines {漆|しつ} (lacquer) and {黒|こく} (black).

USAGE:
- Used almost exclusively as a modifier before a noun: {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ + noun
- Common with ⟦{闇|やみ}→闇：14528_yami⟧ (darkness), ⟦{髪|かみ}→髪：02196_kami⟧ (hair), ⟦{夜空|よぞら}→夜空：09591_yozora⟧ (night sky), ⟦{瞳|ひとみ}→瞳：02252_hitomi⟧ (eyes)
- Has a literary, poetic feel — not typically used in everyday casual speech
- Often found in novels, poetry, and fantasy/game contexts

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{闇|やみ}→闇：14528_yami⟧: pitch-black darkness
- {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{髪|かみ}→髪：02196_kami⟧: jet-black hair
- {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧: pitch-dark night
- {漆黒|しっこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{瞳|ひとみ}→瞳：02252_hitomi⟧: jet-black eyes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}→真っ黒：07614_makkuro⟧: completely black — everyday, casual equivalent
- ⟦{暗黒|あんこく}→暗黒：12997_ankoku⟧: total darkness — emphasizes the absence of light rather than the color
- {墨色|すみいろ}: ink black — another literary color term, slightly softer
